title: Moustache Galapedes and the Vieux Colombier
summary: Moore met Moustache at the 1949 festival, later played with him, and worked the Vieux Colombier with Albert Nicholas.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I see. Well, one of the contemporaries of Sidney was a gentleman in France who you played with by the name of Moustache. How do you pronounce his name, his last name, Francois?
His real name -- he's a Greek but he's been in Paris for many years now. He was born there, but he's of Greek descent and his name is Francois Galapedes.
But he used the word Moustache because he's recognized as a good drummer and that's Moustache.
How actually did you meet him and become fast friends with him?

It was during that original jazz festival when he was supporting Bechet with Claude Luter and the summer of -- I think it was '55, '56, he came to me and asked me if I would join his band. At that time I was with Mezz Mezzrow. Mezz Mezzrow was

going to take the band, his band, an American band, to Canuck, Belgium, another gambling casino on the North Sea.

Yes, Canuck. But I skipped the band and went with Moustache for the summer and that's how I ended up in the Palm Beach Casino in Cannes and it was the most beautiful and wonderful experience of the whole summer. And then from there I had a contract, I was on my way back to NewYork and I received a wire from Vieux Columbier on the Left Bank for me to appear there, too, before I went back to New York. So when I left Cannes, I went back to Paris and worked with Vieux Columbier and one of the fellas that worked there was Albert Nicholas and he was a friend of mine. So I suggested to the owner of the Vieux Columbier that this fellow here was one of the greatest in the east. I was surprised to hear, well, we know of Albert Nicholas.
So why don't we make this job, the more and the merrier. Would you let him come with me? And so the owner of the Vieux Columbier said, no, I think that we'll do it this way. Now you have an identity

I must say Albert Nicholas was a beautiful man. To this day, I relish Albert Nicholas but unfortunately at this time he had passed away, just like Bechet did.
